# Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 42 (Bu-Vb Pc42)

**ID:** Bu-Vb Pc42
**Section:** Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga (bu-vb)
**Collection:** Vinaya
**Title (Pali):** Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 42
**Title (English, from literature):** Dismissing a monk during almsround

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Uyyojanasikkhāpada* constitutes the forty-second rule in the Pācittiya section of the *Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga* within the Pali Vinaya Piṭaka. According to the canonical definition, the rule establishes that if a monk takes another monk along into a village on an almsround and subsequently dismisses him—sending him away because he desires to act inappropriately or engage in misbehavior in private—he incurs an offense requiring confession (*pācittiya*). A complete modern English translation has been prepared by Bhikkhu Brahmali.

The rule has extensive canonical and sectarian parallels across the surviving Vinaya traditions. Within the Pali Vinaya, it is directly formulated in the *Bhikkhu Pātimokkha* (Pācittiya 42) and summarized in the *Parivāra*, with an explicit counterpart in the nun's discipline at *Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga* Pācittiya 123 and *Bhikkhunī Pātimokkha* Pācittiya 123. Beyond Theravāda literature, parallel rules for both monks and nuns are preserved in the Sanskrit, Chinese, and Tibetan recensions of the Sarvāstivāda (Pc 51), Mūlasarvāstivāda (Pc 51), Mahīśāsaka (Pc 76), Mahāsāṅghika and Lokottaravāda (Pc 44), Dharmaguptaka (Pc 46), and Kāśyapīya traditions.

Text-reuse analyses generated by DharmaNexus illustrate that the rule shares widespread stock Vinaya phraseology and analytical legal definitions with other sections of the *Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga*—most notably Pācittiyas 45, 46, 55, 59, 61, 64, 76, and 77—as well as sub-commentarial texts such as the *Vinayavinicchayaṭīkā* and the *Kaṅkhāvitaraṇīpurāṇa-ṭīkā* [DharmaNexus]. Furthermore, DharmaNexus records automated alignments with Tibetan translations of canonical and exegetical Vinaya works, including the *Vinayottaragrantha* (D0007A), the *Pratimokṣabhāṣyāsampramuṣitasmaraṇamātralekha* (D4108), and the *Pratimokṣasūtraṭīkāvinayasamuccaya* (D4106) [DharmaNexus].
